$comment: Deployment targets for scripts/build-deploy.mjs — run `npm run deploy -- <target>`.
platform  "vercel" builds a full Next app: route handlers run, images are
optimised, headers and redirects come from next.config.ts, and the
forms POST /api/leads. Nothing is uploaded — Vercel builds from the
repository, so the script prints the environment it needs instead.
"apache" builds a static export for cPanel: no server, forms POST
the PHP script, headers and redirects come from .htaccess.
siteUrl   Absolute origin INCLUDING any subdirectory, no trailing slash.
Canonical tags, hreflang, Open Graph and the sitemap derive from it.
basePath  The subdirectory alone, or "" at a domain root. A build made for one
prefix cannot be served from another: every asset URL is baked in.
noindex   Sends X-Robots-Tag: noindex on every response. True for any address
that is not the one the brand is meant to be found at.
leads     Where the forms deliver. On apache these are written into
api/leads.php; on vercel they are printed as environment variables,
because a Node build reads them at runtime rather than at build time.
`from` MUST be a mailbox on a domain verified with the mail provider,
or the message fails SPF and is filed as spam.

vercel.label: cwater-claude.vercel.app — live host (Node)
vercel.$note: noindex stays true until a real domain is attached: a *.vercel.app copy of the whole site would compete with cw-eg.com in search. Once cw-eg.com points at Vercel, set siteUrl to https://cw-eg.com and noindex to false.
